summary: CCC-built Hamma Hamma guard station in Olympic National Forest, planned in 1936 as a combined guard station and lookout; still standing and rented as a Forest Service cabin.

facts.design: Single-story CCC guard station with a hexagonal bay window in the living room; 1936 plans called it a combined guard station and lookout
facts.agency: USDA Forest Service, Olympic National Forest

access.note: Rented to guests as a Forest Service cabin. A short gated road leads up to it, and the gate may or may not be open. Visitors who are not guests should check with the Forest Service before going.

visit.trail_note: The Living Legacy (Living Legend) trail follows the Hamma Hamma River from the cabin, 1.8 miles round trip, with signs about the CCC.

events.note: Constructed by the CCC in 1936-37 as the guard station
Planning letter for a combined forest guard station and lookout; the proposed design pushed the living room out toward the brow of the bench to provide visibility
Planning papers describe a guard on patrol who had to leave duty to unlock the fire-season gate below the station

corrections.why: The Forest Fire Lookout Association Washington list classes this lookout as Ground, and the duplicate record already says ground.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The duplicate record notes that firelookout.com does not list it on its standing map. The Forest Service page and WillhiteWeb both describe the building as standing and rented to guests, so it is treated as standing.

notes_for_editor: Two records describe this lookout: us-wa-hamma-hamma-g-s (this one; kind unknown, county unset) and us-wa-hamma-hamma-gs (kind ground, Mason; its status conflict is from firelookout.com). Recommend merging, keeping the Mason county and ground kind. The lookout function rests mainly on WillhiteWeb, a fan site that cites 2019 National Archives documents, and on the FFLA list classing it as Ground. The Forest Service page does not mention an observation room. The FS page says the building was nominated to the NRHP; no listing record was found, so the story says so. WillhiteWeb's quote marks are garbled in the cached text, so quotes there were taken without them. No fire history found. Search snippets from recreation.gov and Revisit WA say the cabin was completed in 1937 and rents year-round; those pages were not read, so they are not cited. The story advises booking or asking the Forest Service rather than visiting unannounced.
